meta.location: The land south and the land north, and Zarahemla
meta.unit: The rise of the Gadianton band (Helaman 1–6)
principles: Prosperity without war as a test
A thing handed down from generation to generation

world_behind.title: The Lamanites are now the more righteous people
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives the reason as firmness and steadiness in the faith, and verse 2 names Nephites who had become hardened and impenitent. Jacob 3:5 had made a narrower version of the same comparison four hundred years earlier, and Helaman 15:4 to 8 will make it again through Samuel.

world_behind.title: Missionaries travel both directions
world_behind.text: Verse 4 has Lamanites preaching in Zarahemla, and verse 6 has Nephi and Lehi going north along with many Lamanites.

world_behind.title: The borders are open
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 8 have both peoples traveling and trading freely anywhere in the land. Alma 22:33 describes the older arrangement, Nephite guards and armies hemming the Lamanites in on the south; this is the first stretch in the record where that line is simply open.

world_behind.title: The record names the two great land divisions
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says the south was called Lehi and the north Mulek, after the son of Zedekiah whom the Lord brought there. Omni 1:15 has the people of Zarahemla coming out of Jerusalem when Zedekiah was carried to Babylon, and Helaman 8:21 asks whether the seed of Zedekiah is not with them. This verse is where the two landings get names on a map.

world_behind.title: Two chief judges are murdered in one year
world_behind.text: Verse 15 has Cezoram killed by an unknown hand on the seat, and his son killed after being appointed in his place. Helaman 1:9 records Pahoran murdered on the same seat by Kishkumen twenty-five years before, so the office has now taken three assassinations in a generation.

world_behind.title: The band operates by signs and a private law
world_behind.text: Verses 22 through 24 describe secret signs and words, mutual protection, and trials held under the laws of their own wickedness. Alma 37:27 and 29 had commanded Helaman to keep the oaths themselves from the people while making their wickedness known, and Ether 8:20 has Moroni refusing to write them for the same reason.

world_behind.title: Mormon traces the oaths past Gadianton
world_behind.text: Verses 26 through 30 name the source as the being who worked with Eve, with Cain, and with the people of the tower.

words.text: Refusing to repent. The record uses the word twice, at Alma 47:36 of Nephite dissenters and here of Nephites who reject the preaching. The King James Bible has it once, at Romans 2:5.
Free movement and dealing between peoples. The word occurs once in scripture, here, and the verse defines it as going where they would, to buy, to sell, and to get gain.

To draw fiber into thread. The record uses the word three times, and the King James Bible three, including the lilies that toil not. Verse 13 gives it to the women, with toil, cloth, and fine-twined linen.
Treated at 2 Nephi 2:16, of the agency by which men act. The record uses the word five times. Verse 26 applies it to what was done to the first parents.
Readiness, absence of resistance. The record uses the word three times, including Alma 37:46 of the easiness of the way. Verse 36 gives it as the reason the Spirit was poured out on the Lamanites.
Led away from allegiance. The word occurs once in the record and nine times in the King James Bible. Verse 38 has the band seducing the more part of the righteous into partaking of the spoils.

phrases.term: Their righteousness did exceed that of the Nephites
phrases.text: The reversal stated flatly in the chapter's first verse. Mormon gives the cause as firmness and steadiness rather than any single event.

phrases.term: They did have free intercourse one with another, to buy and to sell, and to get gain
phrases.text: The peace described as commerce. Two peoples who had fought for nineteen chapters now travel and trade wherever they like.

phrases.term: The land south was called Lehi, and the land north was called Mulek
phrases.text: The record naming its own map. Both names come from the men the Lord brought to each place, and Mulek is identified as a son of Zedekiah.

phrases.term: Their women did toil and spin, and did make all manner of cloth
phrases.text: One of the record's few notices of women's work. It sits in a list of grain, flocks, herds, and refined ore, at the height of the prosperity.

phrases.term: Cezoram was murdered by an unknown hand as he sat upon the judgment-seat
phrases.text: The third chief judge killed in office since Helaman 1. Verse 19 names the band, and adds that they were not found.

phrases.term: They began to seek to get gain that they might be lifted up one above another
phrases.text: Mormon's account of how a peaceful generation went wrong. Long blessing without war left the riches, and the riches became rank.

phrases.term: According to the laws of their wickedness
phrases.text: The band's own judicial system, applied to members who talked. Verse 24 says the laws had been given by Gadianton and Kishkumen.

phrases.term: It is these secret oaths and covenants which Alma commanded his son should not go forth
phrases.text: Mormon identifying the material Alma had sealed in Alma 37:27. The reader learns that the reserved portion of the record was about this.

phrases.term: Those secret oaths and covenants did not come forth unto Gadianton from the records
phrases.text: Mormon closing off the obvious explanation. Alma's restriction held, and the oaths arrived by another route entirely.

phrases.term: He is the author of all sin
phrases.text: The conclusion of the trace. Verse 30 says the plots and oaths are handed from generation to generation as far as he can get hold of hearts.

phrases.term: They did obtain the sole management of the government
phrases.text: The end point of the chapter. The band that fled into the wilderness in Helaman 2:11 now runs the country and tramples the poor and the meek.

verses.label: v. 7–12
verses.title: An open border, described by a pair
verses.text: The passage on free travel is built from three words used in a tight block. North, south and both each stand five times, and all fifteen uses fall between verses 9 and 12. Nothing else in the chapter uses them. The construction is deliberate: gold and silver "in both these lands," grain raised "both in the north and in the south," flourishing "both in the north and in the south." A period of peace is reported not by describing it but by refusing, for four verses, to say anything about one side without saying the same about the other.

verses.label: v. 10
verses.title: A place name that contradicts three biblical verses
verses.text: The record explains the land north's name in passing: it "was called Mulek, which was after the son of Zedekiah; for the Lord did bring Mulek into the land north." The Bible says three times that Zedekiah's sons were killed in front of him, at 2 Kings 25:7, Jer. 39:6 and Jer. 52:10. The volume knows this is a problem and raises it itself two chapters later, at Hel. 8:21. Here the claim is dropped into a sentence about geography, as an aside explaining why a region is called what it is called.

verses.label: v. 15
verses.title: A murder with no one attached to it
verses.text: The chief judge dies in a clause that supplies everything but the murderer: "Cezoram was murdered by an unknown hand as he sat upon the judgment-seat." Unknown hand occurs once in the volume, here. His son, appointed in his place, is killed as well. In a chapter that will spend six verses tracing the origin of secret oaths back to Cain, the one killing it reports leaves the agent blank, and the record does not fill it in later.

verses.label: v. 22–24
verses.title: The machinery of the band, given in detail
verses.text: The record supplies the working parts of the society rather than describing it in general terms: "they did have their signs, yea, their secret signs, and their secret words," and the purpose is that a member "might distinguish a brother who had entered into the covenant." Then verse 24 states the penalty and, more to the point, the jurisdiction: an informer "should be tried, not according to the laws of their country." What makes the band dangerous, in the record's account, is not violence but a parallel court.

verses.label: v. 25–30
verses.title: The record clears its own archive
verses.text: Verse 25 identifies the oaths as the ones "which Alma commanded his son should not go forth unto the world," a reference to an instruction the volume gave at Alma 37. Verse 26 then rules out the obvious inference: "those secret oaths and covenants did not come forth unto Gadianton from the records which were delivered unto Helaman." Having denied the archive as a source, the record supplies another one across four verses, naming Cain and the tower and repeating "that same being" four times. A writer who is himself the custodian of those records stops the narrative to say the leak did not come from them.

chapter.title: The peoples exchange places in one chapter
chapter.text: Verse 1 has the Lamanites more righteous and verse 39 has the Nephite government run by robbers. Mormon marks the crossing with three "thus we see" statements in verses 34 through 36.

chapter.title: Peace and wealth do the damage that war did not
chapter.text: Verse 17 says the Lord had blessed them so long that they were not stirred up to war, and that this is when they set their hearts on riches.

chapter.title: The same band gets opposite treatment
chapter.text: The Lamanites hunt and preach and destroy it. The Nephites build it up and join it. Verses 37 and 38 place the two responses side by side.

chapter.title: The band becomes a rival legal system
chapter.text: Signs, words, mutual immunity, and trials under its own law. Verse 24 describes a government inside the government before verse 39 has it take the real one.

chapter.title: Mormon rules out the record as the source
chapter.text: Verse 26 says the oaths did not come from the plates delivered to Helaman. Alma's restriction in Alma 37 had held.

chapter.title: The trace runs back to Eden
chapter.text: Verses 26 through 29 name Eve, Cain, the tower, and the Jaredites as stops on one line, with Gadianton as the current holder.

chapter.title: Handing down is the mechanism
chapter.text: Verse 30 says the plots and oaths pass from generation to generation as hearts allow. The record has been describing inheritance of records and traditions all along, and this is the dark version.

chapter.title: The victims are named last
chapter.text: Verse 39 ends on the poor, the meek, and the humble followers of God, trampled and smitten and turned away from. The political summary closes with who pays.

applications.title: Notice who is steady rather than who is impressive
applications.text: The Lamanites are called more righteous for firmness and steadiness. Consistency over time is the measure the record uses.

applications.title: Let the people you taught come teach you
applications.text: Lamanite converts came down into Zarahemla and declared to the Nephites the manner of their own conversion. Someone you once helped is often the only person who can say the thing you have stopped being able to hear from your own side.

applications.title: An opening has to run both ways
applications.text: The record has Nephites going wherever they would among the Lamanites and Lamanites doing the same among the Nephites, and the peace and the trade rest on both halves. Traffic permitted in one direction is not an opening and will not produce what an opening produces.

applications.title: Watch yourself in the good years
applications.text: Nothing was attacking them, and that is when they turned. Long stretches without pressure ask a different kind of attention than hard ones.

applications.title: Be wary of a group that judges its own
applications.text: A member who exposed the band was to be tried under the laws of their wickedness rather than the laws of the country. Any group that builds a private court for its own people has decided which rules it means to be out from under.

applications.title: Value being easy to convince
applications.text: Mormon credits the outpouring of the Spirit on the Lamanites to their easiness and willingness to believe. Resisting persuasion can feel like rigor, and this verse treats readiness as the thing that let the change land.

applications.title: Deal with it early or you will host it
applications.text: One people hunted the band and one supported it. The difference in outcome is total, and the moment of choice was early.

applications.title: Ask who gets trampled
applications.text: Mormon ends his political account on the poor and the meek. When judging any arrangement, look at what it does to the people with the least leverage.

questions.text: What freedom am I enjoying that a previous generation fought for?
Whose ordinary daily work is holding up my situation?
What has gone well so long that I have stopped watching it?
What group do I protect regardless of what its members do?
What was handed to me that I would not have chosen?
What have I been seduced into by being offered a share?
